clue.text: Sustain note on organ

parts.note: B is a musical note in the scale
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Keeping a note going on a church organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a weight or burden is to carry it, to support it.

clue.text: Hasn't a place in front, being second matter for consideration

definitions.text: Hasn't a place in front, being second matter for consideration

parts.words: Hasn't a place in front, being second matter for consideration
parts.note: something kept to the back, out of the foreground, is a secondary issue rather than the main business

explanation.surface: An item relegated on an agenda, not at the front but a secondary matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Something that stays at the back rather than at the front, and is of secondary importance, is in the scenery behind the main subject; the clue describes that position two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting and context lie behind the main subject, not up front, and are considered only secondarily.

clue.text: A processed oil I use for mayonnaise

indicators.note: processed suggests the letters of oil are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: blend oil to make a mayonnaise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges only OIL, into IOL; A and I stand as they are either side.
explanation.definitionFit: This Provençal garlic sauce is a kind of mayonnaise.

clue.text: Tried desperately to put rope round — a good effort!

indicators.note: put ... round means the rope goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a cable is a thick rope

indicators.note: done desperately, the letters of tried are flung about into a new order

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who struggled to get a rope around something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' scrambles the letters of the first word, and 'put ... round' wraps the rope around them; the closing exclamation is the definition, praising the attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A praiseworthy attempt deserves credit, which is exactly what this adjective conveys.

clue.text: With regard to the children — send them out again

parts.note: re is a formal word meaning concerning or with regard to
issue means offspring, a person's children

explanation.surface: A note about the children: send them out to play again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' is part of the definition, standing for whatever is being put out again.
explanation.definitionFit: To put out a publication or stamp a second time is to release it once more.

clue.text: He did a right turn? He never changes tack!

indicators.note: turn tells us the letters are turned around into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A sailor who swung right is mocked as one who never alters course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' scrambles HE DID A plus R; a sailing turn would be a change of tack, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A die-hard is a stubborn person who refuses ever to shift position.

clue.text: Noise gnat will start to make

indicators.note: the letters are to be made into a new arrangement, a recipe-style signal to rearrange
the start of the word will is its first letter

explanation.surface: An insect is about to start making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will start' gives W, which joins GNAT; 'to make' rearranges the five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a sharp vibrating sound, as from a plucked string.

clue.text: Surrounded by insects, girl takes first gin, and drinks

indicators.note: surrounded by tells us the girl and the letter go inside the insects

parts.note: bees are insects
Vera is a girl's name

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of gin

explanation.surface: A woman among a swarm of bees has a gin first, then other drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrounded by insects' looks like scenery, but it is the container: the girl and the first letter of gin go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverages are drinks of any kind, apart from water usually.

clue.text: Sell damaged lengths of cloth

indicators.note: damaged signals that the letters of sell are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A trader sells damaged bolts of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old measure for cloth, about forty-five inches in England.

clue.text: Order duck for the military group

parts.note: to command is to order
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: An officer orders a duck dinner for the army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a unit of soldiers trained for raids.

clue.text: Two-by-two creature?

parts.note: suggests an animal on Noah's ark, but means a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs, which shares its name with a reptile

explanation.surface: An animal boarding Noah's Ark in pairs.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs is named after a large reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The reptile's name is also British for a procession of pupils walking two by two.

clue.text: Terrible Ivan will end at the block

indicators.note: terrible, as in Ivan the Terrible, tells us his name is mangled
the end of will is its final letter

explanation.surface: Ivan the Terrible will meet his end at the executioner's block.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges IVAN into ANVI, and 'will end' adds L.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block a smith hammers on.

clue.text: Ghastly-sounding story teller

indicators.note: sounding tells us we want a word that sounds like the one meaning ghastly

parts.note: grim means ghastly or forbidding

explanation.surface: A teller of horror stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brothers Grimm collected German folk and fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Either of the German brothers famous for collecting fairy tales.

clue.text: Following trail on the ground, guns back-track, to get deer

indicators.note: back-track tells us the joined pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a drag is a scent trail dragged over the ground for hounds
gat is slang for a gun, so gats are guns

explanation.surface: Hunters follow a trail and backtrack with their guns to find a deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the guns after the trail, and 'back-track' then reverses the whole run. Drag hunting follows an artificial scent trail laid on the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A staggard is a red deer stag in its fourth year.

clue.text: Bullied and knocked over the head?

definitions.meaning: intimidated by stern looks or words
taken literally, struck on the forehead

explanation.definitionFit: Someone cowed by threats has been intimidated; read literally, the compound means struck on the forehead.

clue.text: Crime of being a receiver?

parts.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods

explanation.surface: Is it criminal to be a receiver?
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; a fence is someone who receives and sells stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of law, a criminal act.

clue.text: Crumbling grotto in the marsh is overlooked

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is a marsh

indicators.note: crumbling tells us the grotto falls apart, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A ruined grotto in the marshland is neglected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' rearranges the grotto's letters, and 'in' places them inside the marsh. Fens are low marshy land, notably in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overlooked has been missed or not remembered.

clue.text: Widow urging one to take a gamble

parts.note: an emphatic do, as in do come, urges someone to act
a wager is a bet or gamble

explanation.surface: A widow is egged on to place a bet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an exhortation, 'Do wager!' urges someone to bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband.

clue.text: Bird seen when Scottish island is gripped by unusual thaw

indicators.note: gripped by means the island goes inside the rearranged letters
unusual signals the letters of thaw appear in an unusual order

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A bird spotted on a Scottish island during a strange thaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of thaw, and 'is gripped by' puts the island inside them. 'Inch' is a Scottish term for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The whinchat is a small brown songbird of open country.

clue.text: Apprehensive and troubled over lying in sun, in retirement

indicators.note: retirement is going back, so the whole is read backwards
lying in places the rearranged letters within the sun
troubled tells us the letters of over are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A retired person, uneasy and worried about sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' makes OVRE from OVER; 'lying in' puts it in SUN to give SUOVREN, and 'in retirement' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous means anxious and fearful about what may happen.

clue.text: Get green stuff in for the sultan

parts.note: salad is leafy green food

explanation.surface: Buy some vegetables in for the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century sultan of Egypt and Syria who fought the crusaders.

clue.text: British parliamentarian observed two-way defeat in America

parts.note: a whip is an MP who enforces party discipline
saw is the past tense of see, observed

explanation.surface: A British MP saw a defeat on two fronts in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament a whip is the party official who makes members vote as the party wants.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage, to beat someone in two ways at once, as in a two-sided loss.

clue.text: Raw fear it engenders?

indicators.note: engenders means produces, so the letters of the two words produce something new

explanation.surface: Fighting breeds naked terror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engenders' rearranges RAW FEAR; the whole clue also describes what armed conflict brings.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict between nations is what produces such terror.

clue.text: He assembles police and Marines on rampage

indicators.note: on a rampage the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A man gathers up police and marines who have run riot.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for the Royal Marines; 'on rampage' scrambles POLICE with RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A compiler gathers material together, as the setter of a crossword puts the clues together.

clue.text: Religious books first-class -— uplifting -—— primate found .

indicators.note: in a down light, uplifting means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of religious books
top means first-class, the best

explanation.surface: Scripture of the highest quality, inspiring, with an ape thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' reverses OTTOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The potto is a slow-moving African primate related to lorises.

clue.text: Telegram from shipping line

definitions.meaning: a heavy rope or chain for mooring a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: Both an overseas wired message and a ship's strong mooring rope or chain.

clue.text: Pickle with cheese taken around noon

indicators.note: taken around means the cheese surrounds the letter

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese

explanation.surface: Pickle with some cheese at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: N for noon goes inside BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Salty water used for preserving food in a pickling solution.

clue.text: Narrative content of many miniature pictures

indicators.note: content of signals letters contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A story told by a collection of small paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'miniaturE PICtures'.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long heroic poem or story.

clue.text: Dog, perhaps. it is very small

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

explanation.surface: Is it a dog? It is tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Petit is French for little, used in English for tiny things.

clue.text: Mad artist battered writer

indicators.note: battered means the letters are knocked about into new positions

explanation.surface: A crazed painter was beaten up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist is a writer of plays.

clue.text: Perplexed to discover firm originated in the north

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
N is short for north
founded means set up, originated

explanation.surface: Puzzled to find a company started up in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word placing N within the run of pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Confounded means baffled, utterly confused.

clue.text: Haunt of vice in which you'll see a church dignitary

indicators.note: in which you'll see means a letter can be seen inside the haunt

parts.note: a den is a haunt of vice, as in den of iniquity

explanation.surface: A clergyman spotted in a den of iniquity.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dean heads the chapter of a cathedral.
